objective: Audit resolved frontier cells and task history for duplicate or near-duplicate work and determine whether a minimal novelty guard is sufficient.
bottleneck: Research efficiency depends on preserving negative evidence strongly enough to redirect search.
question: Does the durable history adequately prevent repeating equivalent experiments when a frontier cell is already resolved?
action: Audited the durable frontier (state/LEARNING_STATE.md), persistent state (state/STATE.md), the campaign queue and its selection semantics (state/campaign/task_queue.json, state/campaign/runs/43181285853/campaign_status.json, .github/scripts/campaign_controller.py::candidate_tasks_for_role/task_rank), the research check inventory (research/checks/), and the artifact inventory (state/check_artifacts/). Mapped every resolved frontier cell to its executing check and artifact, then inspected candidate near-duplicate pairs by construction and by tested parameter coverage: cross_sectional_relative_strength.py vs cross_sectional_momentum.py (same construction, lookback 20 vs 63) and momentum_sweep.py vs momentum_lookback_sweep.py (same lookback-sweep objective, lookbacks 3/5/10/20 vs 3/5/10). No historical experiment was rerun.

Near-duplicate pair A confirmed from artifacts: cross_sectional_relative_strength_results.json (lookback 20, top_k 3, overall_verdict REGIME_STABLE but per-sub-universe CONSISTENT_WITH_NOISE=9/REGIME_STABLE=1-negative, NO_EDGE concentration; perturbation lookbacks 10/20/40) and cross_sectional_momentum_results.json (lookback 63, top_k 3, CONSISTENT_WITH_NOISE; perturbation lookbacks 21/63/126). Same construction (rank cross-section by past lookback return; long top-k / short bottom-k; hold 1 day; daily rebalance) and same gate stack; the 63-day cell was executed after the 20-day cell was already FALSIFIED.

Near-duplicate pair B confirmed from source and git history: research/checks/momentum_sweep.py declares LOOKBACKS=(3,5,10,20) and writes momentum_sweep_results.json, while research/checks/momentum_lookback_sweep.py declares LOOKBACKS=(3,5,10) and writes the retained momentum_lookback_sweep_results.json; the momentum_sweep artifact is absent from the current working tree, so the 3/5/10/20 sweep is a superseded near-duplicate check.

Controller selector semantics read at .github/scripts/campaign_controller.py: candidate_tasks_for_role filters only on role and status=='OPEN'; the task schema (REQUIRED_TASK_FIELDS) has no novelty or construction-signature field, so the queue cannot detect a newly added OPEN task that duplicates a RESOLVED cell.

observed_effect: Equivalent (verbatim) experiments are not repeated: every resolved frontier cell maps to exactly one executed check + one artifact, and no task has been selected twice. Near-duplicate parameter extensions do occur: (A) the cross-sectional construction was executed at lookback 20 (FALSIFIED) and again at lookback 63 (FALSIFIED) even though the 20-day cell's perturbation sweep already covered lookbacks 10/20/40, and (B) a superseded 3/5/10/20 momentum lookback sweep (momentum_sweep.py) coexists with the retained 3/5/10 sweep (momentum_lookback_sweep.py). Both near-duplicates were low-cost and produced corroborating, independently verified FALSIFIED evidence, and neither blocked search redirection. The controller queue has no checkable novelty guard, but the observed near-duplicates arose at authoring time (new check files), not at queue selection, so a queue-level guard alone would not have caught them.
uncertainty_targeted: Whether the durable history adequately prevents repeating equivalent experiments when a frontier cell is already resolved, and whether a minimal novelty guard is needed.
uncertainty_reduced: Resolved for equivalent experiments: the durable history (frontier table + one-artifact-per-cell convention + queue status transitions) does prevent verbatim re-tests. Narrowed for near-duplicates: a real but low-rate residual exists at the authoring stage, quantified as two cases (cross-sectional 20 vs 63; superseded momentum sweep), both corroborating rather than search-blocking.
research_result: No research experiment was run; this is a process audit. The durable history prevents equivalent experiments (each resolved cell has exactly one executed artifact; no task re-selected) and successfully redirects search to a new class after each resolved cell. Near-duplicate parameter extensions were observed (cross-sectional lookback 20 vs 63; a superseded 3/5/10/20 momentum sweep) but were low-cost and yielded corroborating FALSIFIED evidence, so the current near-duplicate rate does not constitute a material bottleneck. The existing novelty rule (LEARNING_STATE learning rule 2 and LEARNING_EFFICIENCY.md section 2) plus the frontier table is adequate at this rate; a minimal novelty guard is not justified as a new mechanism now and is recorded as a conditional candidate task (P-008) should near-duplicates recur.

candidate_tasks.primary_question: If a future activation records another near-duplicate of an already-resolved frontier cell, is one checkable construction-signature field sufficient to prevent it?
candidate_tasks.bottleneck: The frontier records each cell in prose but has no checkable field naming the prior resolved cell and the concrete differing objective, so near-duplicate parameter extensions can pass the novelty rule on a loosely-claimed different objective.
candidate_tasks.objective: Add one checkable construction-signature field to the frontier schema and require each new cell to name the prior resolved cell it differs from and the concrete differing information objective.
candidate_tasks.scope: state/LEARNING_STATE.md frontier schema plus one learning rule; no controller changes and no new experiments.
candidate_tasks.out_of_scope: Do not modify .github/workflows or .github/scripts, do not add a broad metadata system or numeric score, and do not rerun historical experiments.
candidate_tasks.deliverable: A minimal schema/rule change with a worked example applied to the cross-sectional cells, validated by the controller record gate.
candidate_tasks.success_criterion: The field is present, the rule is stated, and the worked example is reproducible from durable state.
candidate_tasks.stop_condition: Stop after the single field and rule are added and validated.
candidate_tasks.verification_requirement: Controller-side validation of the durable record and markdown structure; no research experiment.
candidate_tasks.evidence_basis: This activation (P-002) found near-duplicate cross-sectional cells (lookback 20 and 63) executed after the first was resolved FALSIFIED, and a superseded 3/5/10/20 momentum lookback sweep.
